payroll-update.reveal_note: Both emails look professional, but the fake's sender and link domain (meridianfreiqht.com) swaps the g in 'freight' for a q -- easy to miss at a glance, which is exactly the point.
red_flags: Sender and link domain meridianfreiqht.com (q instead of g)
Link goes to a subdomain of the lookalike domain
payroll-update.what_you_can_do: Check payroll changes in the HR system yourself, or ask Payroll on a channel you trust.

shared-document.reveal_note: The fake's "shared document" link doesn't go to the real file-sharing provider at all -- it points to an unrelated domain disguised to look like one, a common way to harvest login credentials through a fake sign-in page.
red_flags: Sender domain clouddocs-share.net is not clouddocs.com
Link goes to a login page over plain http
shared-document.what_you_can_do: Message Priya on a channel you trust before opening a shared link you didn't expect.

software-renewal.reveal_note: The fake's invoice total and "past due" framing are meant to create urgency, the payment link goes to a generic lookalike domain rather than the vendor's own billing portal, and the attached "invoice" has a double file extension (.pdf.exe) -- a classic sign it's an executable, not a document.
red_flags: Sender domain designsuite-billing.net is not designsuite.com
'Past due' and service suspended in 48 hours
Attachment ends in .pdf.exe: it's a program, not a document
Payment link goes to the lookalike domain
software-renewal.what_you_can_do: Check invoices in the vendor's own portal, and never open a file ending .pdf.exe.

docusign-review.subject_label: A DocuSign request from a colleague
docusign-review.reveal_note: The fake keeps the colleague's name, but its address is docusign-secure-view.co, not docusign.net, and it adds a 2-hour expiry. Its link opens a page asking for your work email password.
red_flags: Sender domain docusign-secure-view.co is not docusign.net
Link goes to a different domain over plain http
The page asks for your work email password, which DocuSign never needs to view a document
docusign-review.what_you_can_do: Check with Alicia on a channel you trust, or open DocuSign yourself, before signing in anywhere.

gdrive-share.subject_label: A Google Drive share from a colleague
gdrive-share.reveal_note: The fake uses goog1e-docs-viewer.com (a digit 1 for the l), not google.com. Its page even shows a padlock, which only means the connection is encrypted, not that the site is genuine.
red_flags: Sender and link domain goog1e-docs-viewer.com (a digit 1 for the 'l')
The page has a padlock, which proves nothing about who runs it
It asks you to sign in again to 'confirm access'
gdrive-share.what_you_can_do: Open Drive from your own bookmark or the app instead of the email link.

singpost-locker.reveal_note: The real QR code is a collection code you show to the locker. The fake asks you to scan a QR code to pay $2.40 within 12 hours, from singpost-collect.top rather than singpost.com, and leads to a card payment page.
red_flags: Sender domain singpost-collect.top is not singpost.com
A QR code that asks you to pay is a warning sign
Blurry banner that reads 'SingP0st' with a zero
The QR hides where it leads
The page asks for card details
singpost-locker.what_you_can_do: Check the parcel on singpost.com or in the SingPost app, never by scanning a code from an email.

invoice-image.reveal_note: The fake is one big picture with no text, which slips past text filters, from adobe-invoice-center.net, with an .html attachment (a common fake-login trick). The real receipt is ordinary text from adobe.com.
red_flags: Sender domain adobe-invoice-center.net is not adobe.com
The whole message is one image: no real text or link
A spelling mistake inside the picture ('becuase')
Threat that the service will be stopped
invoice-image.what_you_can_do: Never open an .html attachment. Check billing in your Adobe account directly.

bank-new-device.subject_label: A bank sign-in alert, on your phone
bank-new-device.reveal_note: On a phone you only see the display name, so both say Harborline Bank. The sender address, behind Details, is harborline-verify.top, not harborlinebank.com. The real alert has no link and tells you to open the app.
red_flags: Sender domain harborline-verify.top is not harborlinebank.com
The link text hides where it goes
The link opens an unrelated site over plain http
bank-new-device.what_you_can_do: On a phone, tap the sender name to see the real address. Don't tap a sign-in link; open the bank's app yourself.

dbs-ibanking.reveal_note: The real alert comes from dbs.com and gives no link. The fake comes from dbs-secure-alerts.com and its link only starts with dbs-secure-alerts.com: the real host is login-verify.top.
red_flags: A big charge to alarm you
dbs-ibanking.what_you_can_do: Never use a link in a bank alert. Open the DBS digibank app or call the number on your card.

ocbc-estatement.subject_label: A bank e-statement, on your phone
ocbc-estatement.reveal_note: The real email comes from ocbc.com and says statements are never sent as attachments. The fake comes from ocbc-estatement.net with an .html attachment, which opens a fake sign-in page.
red_flags: Asks you to sign in from it
ocbc-estatement.what_you_can_do: Never open an .html attachment. Log in to OCBC Online Banking yourself to see statements.

aws-bill.reveal_note: The real email comes from amazon.com and says to use your own bookmark. The fake comes from aws-billing-center.com, claims big unusual charges and links to a look-alike console.
red_flags: A big charge to alarm you
aws-bill.what_you_can_do: Open the AWS console from your own bookmark. Never sign in through an email link.

github-session.subject_label: A GitHub security alert, on your phone
github-session.reveal_note: The real alert comes from github.com and tells you to go to github.com/settings yourself. The fake comes from github-support.co, names a scary location and sets a 1-hour deadline.
github-session.what_you_can_do: Tap the sender name to check the address. Go to github.com yourself and look at your security log.

slack-invite.reveal_note: The real invite comes from slack.com and links to your company's own Slack address. The fake comes from slack-workspace-invite.com and baits you with unread leadership messages.
slack-invite.what_you_can_do: Open Slack from the app or your bookmark. Never sign in from an emailed link.

okta-password.subject_label: An Okta security email, on your phone
okta-password.reveal_note: The real email comes from okta.com and tells you to contact IT if it wasn't you. The fake comes from okta-meridianfreight.com and says your access will be suspended unless you sign in.
okta-password.what_you_can_do: Ask the IT Service Desk through a channel you already trust. IT never resets MFA by link.

booking-card.reveal_note: The real email comes from booking.com and sends you to the app. The fake comes from booking-confirm-pay.com, sets a 6-hour deadline and uses a QR code that hides where it leads.
booking-card.what_you_can_do: Don't scan a QR code from an email. Open the Booking.com app and check the booking there.

sharepoint-share.subject_label: A shared file from a colleague
sharepoint-share.reveal_note: The real notice comes from sharepointonline.com and links to your company's own SharePoint. The fake comes from sharepoint-docs.net and sends you to a sign-in page on another site.
sharepoint-share.what_you_can_do: Open the file from OneDrive or Teams yourself, or message Dana to check it was really sent.

zoom-recording.subject_label: A Zoom recording email, on your phone
zoom-recording.reveal_note: The real email comes from zoom.us and sends you to Recordings in the app. The fake comes from zoom-recordings.net and says the recording will be deleted in 24 hours unless you sign in.
zoom-recording.what_you_can_do: Open the Zoom app and check Recordings yourself. Don't sign in from a link.

apple-receipt.reveal_note: The real receipt comes from apple.com and points to reportaproblem.apple.com. The fake comes from apple-billing-support.com, shows a big charge and tells you to phone a number, where a scammer waits.
red_flags: A big charge to alarm you
Tells you to phone a number
apple-receipt.what_you_can_do: Never phone a number from a receipt. Check purchases in your Apple account yourself.

paypal-invoice.subject_label: A PayPal invoice, on your phone
paypal-invoice.reveal_note: The real email comes from paypal.com and tells you to log in yourself. The fake comes from paypal.com.invoice-pay.top, where paypal.com is only a prefix: the real domain is invoice-pay.top.
paypal-invoice.what_you_can_do: Read a web address from right to left: the domain is just before the first slash. Open PayPal yourself.

google-workspace.subject_label: A Google Workspace alert, on your phone
google-workspace.reveal_note: The real alert comes from google.com and tells you to go to myaccount.google.com yourself. The fake comes from google-workspace-admin.co and threatens to disable your mailbox.
google-workspace.what_you_can_do: Admins don't ask you to sign in from an email. Check with IT through a channel you trust.

sms-ocbc-otp.reveal_note: Both show OCBC: a fake can reuse a genuine sender name. The real text gives you an OTP and a number to call. The fake asks you to type an OTP into ocbc-secure.net.
red_flags: Asks you to hand over an OTP
sms-ocbc-otp.what_you_can_do: Never type an OTP into a website you reached from a text. Real OTPs are for you to use, not to hand over.

sms-iras-refund.reveal_note: The real text points to mytax.iras.gov.sg. The fake's link starts with iras-refunds.gov-sg.top, so its real domain is gov-sg.top, not a .gov.sg address.
sms-iras-refund.what_you_can_do: Government sites end in .gov.sg. Go to mytax.iras.gov.sg yourself and log in with Singpass.

sms-lazada-redeliver.reveal_note: The real text sends you to the Lazada app. The fake claims a failed delivery and links to lazada-redeliver.com.
red_flags: A link instead of the app
sms-lazada-redeliver.what_you_can_do: Open the Lazada app to see delivery status. Don't reschedule through a link in a text.

sms-uob-device.reveal_note: Both show UOB. The real text tells you to call the bank. The fake gives you a link to cancel, at uob-cancel.net.
red_flags: A link replaces the phone call
sms-uob-device.what_you_can_do: Call the number on the back of your card, not a link in the text.

qr-ev-charger.subject_label: A QR code on an EV charger
qr-ev-charger.reveal_note: The real sign sends you to the Shell Recharge app. The fake is a sticker over the original with shell-recharge-pay.com printed on it, and it asks for your card on a web page.
red_flags: A sticker over the real code
Card form on an odd site
qr-ev-charger.what_you_can_do: Use the charging app you installed yourself, not a code on a sticker. Report stickers to building management.

qr-lobby-flyer.subject_label: A QR flyer in the office lobby
qr-lobby-flyer.reveal_note: The real flyer is from IT Security and opens the intranet. The fake offers a free gift card for staff and prints meridianfreight-rewards.com, which is not the company's domain.
qr-lobby-flyer.what_you_can_do: Be wary of unexpected flyers. Ask IT or Facilities before scanning a code on a notice board.

qr-mrt-poster.subject_label: A QR poster at a station
qr-mrt-poster.reveal_note: The real poster sends you to the app store. The fake offers free credit if you log in, and prints grab-sg-promo.top.
qr-mrt-poster.what_you_can_do: Install apps by searching your phone's app store, not by scanning posters.
